$comment: READ-ONLY. The report agent's window onto data quality.
WHY ONLY A READ: every WRITE on the native DQ surface is a bare array body —
POST /monitor, PUT /monitor, PATCH /check — so an HTTP tool cannot create or
change a monitor. DQ standards are worse: no public API at all, and the
internal /api/dq/standards is bare-array AND cookie-authenticated. Scoped and
closed 2026-09-04; see the DQ section in CLAUDE.md. Do not add a create tool
The GET is fine: query parameters, BearerAuth, no body. Verified from the
MONITORS BIND TO COLUMNS, NOT TO CDEs. There is no cde_id field on Monitor or
Check, and no CDE filter on either list endpoint — verified across both
schemas. So the join back to a CDE is done by the CALLER: take the CDE's PDE
source keys (alation://attribute/<id>), and match them against the table_id /
column ids these monitors cover. That join is the whole reason this tool
exists, and it is why the agent must read PDEs before it reads monitors.
name: Fetch DQ Monitors
description: List the data quality monitors configured in this Alation instance, with the tables and columns each one covers, its schedule, priority and owners. Monitors bind to a data source, table and column — never to a Critical Data Element — so to find out whether a CDE is monitored you must match the columns behind its physical data elements against the columns these monitors cover. Read-only: monitors cannot be created or changed through an agent.

ds_id.description: Restrict to one data source, e.g. 2 for MCF Snowflake. Use it — an unscoped read returns every monitor on the instance.

table_ids.description: Restrict to specific tables, by numeric table id.

schema_ids.description: Restrict to specific schemas, by numeric schema id.
